evals.prompt: Tasks for quota alerts are approved. Run the task review on this work item before we start building. requirements.md, design.md and tasks.md are in the working directory, with the shared project docs alongside.
evals.expected_output: The reply should run the task review and write task-review-summary.md for the quota alerts work item with Status APPROVED and no CRITICAL or MAJOR issues (zero or only MINOR suggestions, such as task-splitting advice). The coverage matrix should show all thirteen acceptance criteria (1.1 to 5.2) traced to at least one task, the design coverage table should map every design element (ThresholdSet schema, the GET and PUT thresholds endpoints, ThresholdValidator, ThresholdService, ThresholdsHandler, AlertEvaluator, the quota-threshold template, the ThresholdSettings component and the two data model changes) to tasks, and the sequencing review should record that the OpenAPI update and type regeneration come before the handler and the frontend, backend before frontend, and integration, end-to-end, documentation and final validation tasks come last. The mandatory ending tasks should all be marked present. The verdict should approve and point to sdd:spec-qa-review in plan mode as the next step. Existing-file paths that cannot be checked on disk because only the work item is supplied should not turn into a MAJOR finding.
criteria: Writes task-review-summary.md under the work-item directory with Status APPROVED
Reports zero CRITICAL and zero MAJOR issues
The coverage matrix traces every acceptance criterion from 1.1 to 5.2 to at least one task, with no gap marked
The design coverage table maps each design element to an implementing task
The sequencing review confirms the OpenAPI task precedes the handler and the frontend task
All mandatory ending tasks (integration tests, E2E, documentation, final validation) are marked present
Names sdd:spec-qa-review in plan mode as the next step

evals.prompt: I've signed off tasks.md for quota alerts and want to move on to implementation. Can you run the task review first? The three work item documents are in the working directory.
evals.expected_output: The reply should write task-review-summary.md with Status BLOCKED, because one acceptance criterion has no implementing task and the skill rates missing requirement coverage CRITICAL. The finding must name acceptance criterion 2.4 (no Quota_Alerts for a suspended Account): the AlertEvaluator task traces only 2.1, 2.2 and 2.3 and never mentions the suspended status, and no other task covers it. The coverage matrix should mark AC 2.4 as uncovered while the other twelve criteria are covered, and the statistics should show one CRITICAL issue. The fix should be a specific change to tasks.md, such as adding the suspended-Account check and its unit test to the AlertEvaluator task and tracing 2.4 to it. The verdict should say the work is blocked until tasks.md is fixed and the review re-run. The reply must not approve it or tell the user to proceed to implementation. Sequencing and the ending tasks are sound and should not generate MAJOR findings.
criteria: Writes task-review-summary.md with Status BLOCKED
Raises a CRITICAL finding that names acceptance criterion 2.4 (no alerts for a suspended Account) as having no task
The coverage matrix marks AC 2.4 as uncovered and the other criteria as covered
Gives a specific fix to tasks.md, such as adding the suspended check and a test to the AlertEvaluator task and tracing 2.4
States that tasks.md must be fixed and the review re-run before implementation, and does not approve
Does not invent further CRITICAL or MAJOR findings about sequencing or the ending tasks

evals.prompt: tasks.md for quota alerts is approved and I'd like to start building. Run the task review on it. requirements.md, design.md and tasks.md are in the working directory.
evals.expected_output: The reply should write task-review-summary.md with Status APPROVED WITH ISSUES: every acceptance criterion and design element is covered, so there is no CRITICAL finding, but one MAJOR sequencing finding. In tasks.md the ThresholdSettings frontend task comes second, before the OpenAPI task (which adds the thresholds endpoints and the ThresholdSet schema and regenerates the types) and before ThresholdsHandler. The finding must give the mechanism: the frontend task imports the generated ThresholdSet type, which does not exist until the OpenAPI task has been run and scripts/generate-api-types.sh has regenerated the TypeScript types (types are generated from openapi.yaml, never hand-written), and it calls GET and PUT /accounts/{accountId}/thresholds, which have no handler to call yet, so the build fails and the component cannot be exercised. The fix should be to move the frontend task after the OpenAPI, service and handler tasks (and the checkpoint). The statistics should show one MAJOR and no CRITICAL, and the verdict should allow proceeding once the order is fixed, warning the user rather than blocking outright.
criteria: Writes task-review-summary.md with Status APPROVED WITH ISSUES
Raises a MAJOR sequencing finding that the ThresholdSettings frontend task comes before the OpenAPI task and the handler
Gives the mechanism that the generated ThresholdSet types do not exist yet, so the frontend has nothing to import
Gives the mechanism that the thresholds endpoints have no handler yet, so there is nothing for the component to call
Proposes moving the frontend task after the OpenAPI, service and handler tasks
Reports no CRITICAL issues and shows the coverage matrix fully covered

evals.prompt: Please review tasks.md for the quota alerts work item before we hand it to the subagents. The work item documents are in the working directory.
evals.expected_output: The reply should write task-review-summary.md with Status APPROVED WITH ISSUES: coverage and sequencing are sound, so there is no CRITICAL finding, but the ThresholdsHandler task is not implementable as written, which the skill rates MAJOR. The task tells the developer to map every failure through 'the existing ProblemMapper', a component that design.md does not define and that appears nowhere in the architecture or contract (only the Problem schema exists), and to 'add appropriate error handling for anything else', a vague instruction that gives a subagent nothing to act on. The finding should name the handler task, the undefined ProblemMapper and the vague error-handling phrase, and the fix should be to specify the behaviour concretely (build the standard Problem body for 400 and 404 directly, or add and define a mapper in the design) and to list the exact error cases. The statistics should show at least one MAJOR and no CRITICAL, and the verdict should warn and allow proceeding after the fix.
criteria: Writes task-review-summary.md with Status APPROVED WITH ISSUES
Raises a MAJOR implementability finding on the ThresholdsHandler task
Identifies ProblemMapper as a component that design.md does not define
Identifies 'add appropriate error handling' as an ambiguous instruction
Gives a specific fix, such as stating the Problem body for 400 and 404 directly or defining the mapper in the design
Reports no CRITICAL issues and no sequencing finding
